mcqs.q: What is the difference between overt and covert prestige?
options: It is the stage where children memorise long stories.

Overt prestige is the high status of standard varieties recognised by society (RP, Standard English); covert prestige is the hidden status of non-standard varieties within particular groups, signalling solidarity or toughness.
Only standard language has prestige; non-standard varieties have none.
Overt prestige is loud speech and covert prestige is quiet speech.
Implicature is the same as the literal meaning of a sentence.
It is the stage where children memorise long stories.
Implicature is a kind of grammatical mistake.
Meaning conveyed beyond what is literally said — generated when speakers obey or deliberately flout Grice's maxims. 'Some students passed' implicates 'not all', via the maxim of quantity.
